__inputs.name: DS_PROMETHEUS
__inputs.label: Prometheus
__inputs.description: Prometheus data source scraping the orleans.lattice (and optionally orleans.lattice.replication) meter.

panels.title: Dependency wait p95 (ms) - causal-consistency staging
panels.description: Wait time for entries parked in the causal-apply buffer awaiting dependency satisfaction. Only emits samples when causal staging is enabled AND at least one entry parks. Flat-zero (no series) is the healthy steady state - the 'or vector(0)' guard renders zero rather than 'No data'.

panels.title: Dead-letter queue churn (ops/s)
panels.description: Dead-letter enqueue/removal rate. Only emits when permanent transport or apply failures occur. Flat-zero is the healthy steady state.

panels.title: Apply correctness violations (rate)
panels.description: FIFO and causal-violation counters. A sustained nonzero rate indicates a real correctness regression. Flat-zero is required for a healthy cluster.

panels.title: Peer fell-off-log events (count over range)
panels.description: Receiver fell-off-log detections per peer. Nonzero means the receiver's high-water-mark is older than the sender's oldest WAL entry - i.e. the receiver missed the catch-up window. Flat-zero is the healthy steady state.

panels.title: Apply buffer (entries)
panels.description: Causal-apply buffer occupancy in entries. Only emits when causal staging parks an entry. Flat-zero (or absent) means no causal staging is engaged. When non-zero, see the apply-lag overlay panel for the bistability signal. The matching bytes panel is rendered to the right of this one.

panels.title: Per-peer last outbound ship (seconds ago)
panels.description: Wall-clock seconds since the local sender last successfully shipped a batch (or an empty liveness probe) to the named peer. Filters on direction=outbound; the inbound twin panel renders the receiver-side timeline.

panels.title: Apply lag p99 vs apply-buffer depth (causal-staging bistability overlay)
panels.description: Overlays apply-lag p99 (left axis, ms) against the causal-apply buffer occupancy (right axis, entries). The bistability hypothesis: once the buffer crosses ~N entries, apply-lag p99 stays pegged at a high level for the rest of the window even as the buffer eventually drains. If only the lag panel renders (buffer flat-zero), causal staging is not engaged and the bistability is in a different layer (e.g. shipper backpressure, sender-side WAL). Use this panel as the first stop when the lag-p99 sweep shows wide run-to-run variance.

panels.title: Apply buffer (bytes)
panels.description: Causal-apply buffer occupancy in bytes. Tracks the same lifecycle as the entries panel to its left at byte granularity. Together they bound the buffer against CausalBufferMaxEntries and CausalBufferMaxBytes. Flat-zero (or absent) means no causal staging is engaged.

panels.title: Per-peer bytes behind
panels.description: Cumulative WAL payload bytes the local sender has yet to ship to each peer. Companion to the per-peer entries-behind panel to the left.

panels.title: Per-peer last inbound apply (seconds ago)
panels.description: Wall-clock seconds since the local receiver last successfully applied a batch authored by the named peer. Filters on direction=inbound; symmetric twin of the outbound ship panel.

panels.title: Per-peer negotiated wire version
panels.description: Framing wire version the local sender has negotiated as the target for the named peer (min(localCurrent, peerAdvertised), or the unknown-peer floor until the peer advertises). Capability/telemetry only - the sender does not yet re-encode at this version (see follow-up issue).

panels.title: Per-peer wire-version downgrade active (1 = mixed-version fleet)
panels.description: 1 when the negotiated target version is strictly below the sender's current wire version (a mixed-version fleet during a rolling upgrade), else 0. Telemetry only - reflects the negotiated target, not an actual re-encode.

panels.title: Anti-entropy digest-probe comparisons (rate, by outcome)
panels.description: Per-shard digest comparisons performed by the anti-entropy probe scheduler, by outcome (match / mismatch / version_skew / remote_unavailable). Dark/opt-in: zero unless DigestProbeEnabled is set.

panels.title: Anti-entropy digest divergence (mismatch rate)
panels.description: Per-shard digest comparisons whose versions matched but hashes differed - the local cluster and the named peer have diverged for that shard. Pair with the comparisons panel to compute the divergence ratio. Dark/opt-in.

panels.title: Redundant payload re-send rate
panels.description: Rate of byte-identical content re-sets the shipper observed while content-hash dedup measurement is enabled (ContentHashDedupEnabled). 'entries/s' counts redundant Set entries; 'bytes/s' is the value bytes they carried. Flat-zero unless the workload re-sets identical values for a key. Observability-only - the shipper never elides or reorders bytes on the wire.

panels.title: Effective ship batch size (adaptive)
panels.description: Per-tick outbound batch cap the shipper actually used, distribution p50/p95/p99. With adaptive sizing off (AdaptiveBatchSizingEnabled=false, the default) this sits flat at the configured ShipBatchSize; with it on, the AIMD controller raises it toward ShipBatchSize on a healthy link and backs it off on rising ack latency or send errors. The receiver flow-control hint is always the hard ceiling.

panels.title: Ship ack latency p50/p95/p99 (ms)
panels.description: Round-trip latency from sending a batch to receiving its ack, per (tree, peer). This is the primary signal the adaptive batch-size controller reacts to: a sustained rise above AdaptiveBatchLatencyThreshold shrinks the effective batch size. Emitted on every acknowledged batch regardless of whether adaptive sizing is enabled.

panels.title: Merkle-walk leaves localised (rate)
panels.description: Rate of diverging leaves the read-only anti-entropy Merkle walk narrowed a shard mismatch down to. Opt-in via MerkleWalkEnabled; stays zero unless a range-answering probe transport is wired up.

panels.title: Merkle-walk aborted (rate by reason)
panels.description: Rate of read-only Merkle-walk passes that stopped before localising, split by reason (depth_cap, byte_budget, remote_unavailable, version_skew). With the default transport every triggered walk reports remote_unavailable.

panels.title: Pre-ship coalescing elided rate
panels.description: Rate of redundant per-key versions the shipper dropped from outbound batches by pre-ship coalescing (PreShipCoalescingEnabled, last-writer-wins trees only). 'entries/s' counts elided WAL entries; 'bytes/s' is the pre-encoded wire-segment bytes they carried. Flat-zero unless a hot key is rewritten several times within one ship window. The coalesced output is a strict subset an unmodified receiver converges to identically.

panels.title: Leaf re-replay entries re-shipped (rate)
panels.description: Rate of retained write-ahead-log entries the targeted leaf re-replay repair stage re-shipped to a diverged peer. Opt-in via LeafReReplayEnabled; stays zero unless localisation finds a divergent leaf and a real push transport is wired up.

panels.title: Leaf re-replay skipped (rate by reason)
panels.description: Rate of targeted leaf re-replay passes that skipped without re-shipping, split by reason (disabled, range_empty, wal_trimmed). A wal_trimmed series is the operator-only alert: the local WAL was garbage-collected past the divergence point and a bootstrap-snapshot remediation is required.

panels.title: Apply parallelism - runs per batch
panels.description: Distribution of the receiver apply degree-of-parallelism chosen per batch (orleans.lattice.replication.apply.parallel_runs). 1 = serial apply (the default, or a batch with no independent (tree, origin) runs); higher values appear only when ApplyMaxParallelRuns > 1 and the batch fans out across independent runs.

panels.title: Outbound batches in flight per peer
panels.description: Current count of shipped-but-unacknowledged replication batches per peer (orleans.lattice.replication.peer.ship_in_flight observable gauge). Climbs toward ShipMaxInFlight when pipelining is enabled and the peer is the bottleneck; flat at 0 or 1 with default settings.

panels.title: Bootstrap throughput (rate)
panels.description: Per-tree rate of entries and value bytes received by the receiver bootstrap/backfill path (orleans.lattice.replication.bootstrap.entries_received / bootstrap.bytes_received). Non-zero only while a peer is catching up a cold or fell-off-log receiver.

panels.title: Bootstrap duration p50/p95/p99 (ms)
panels.description: Wall-clock duration of receiver bootstrap operations (orleans.lattice.replication.bootstrap.duration), tagged by origin and outcome. Long tails indicate large backfills or a slow source.

panels.title: Bootstrap transient retries (rate)
panels.description: Rate of transient (retryable) failures during receiver bootstrap (orleans.lattice.replication.bootstrap.transient_retries), by tree. A sustained non-zero rate signals a flaky source link slowing convergence.

panels.title: Fall-off-log suppressed events (rate)
panels.description: Rate of fall-off-log detections suppressed as duplicates (orleans.lattice.replication.peer.fell_off_log_suppressed), by tree. Pairs with the peer.fell_off_log panel: a high suppressed-to-raised ratio means the detector is correctly de-duplicating repeated signals for the same gap.

panels.title: Bootstrap fallback triggered (rate)
panels.description: Rate of scoped bootstrap-snapshot fallback passes that began after a targeted leaf re-replay reported the local write-ahead-log was garbage-collected past the divergence point. Opt-in via BootstrapFallbackEnabled; stays zero unless a wal_trimmed leaf re-replay occurs and the fallback is enabled.

panels.title: Bootstrap fallback entries re-shipped (rate)
panels.description: Rate of committed-projection entries the scoped bootstrap-snapshot fallback re-derived from the live tree and re-shipped to a diverged peer. Opt-in via BootstrapFallbackEnabled; stays zero unless a fallback pass ships at least one entry.

panels.title: Bootstrap fallback skipped (rate by reason)
panels.description: Rate of scoped bootstrap-snapshot fallback passes that skipped without re-shipping, split by reason (disabled, range_empty, empty). A disabled series is the operator-only signal that a wal_trimmed divergence was repairable but the fallback was not opted in.

panels.title: Remediation disabled (tree/peer by reason)
panels.description: Each (tree, peer) for which automatic anti-entropy remediation is currently disabled, valued 1 and split by reason (opt_out, budget_exhausted, circuit_open). opt_out is the steady-state signal that drift was localised but the host has not set AutoRemediateOnDigestMismatch; budget_exhausted means the per-window remediation traffic budget is spent; circuit_open means the per-tree/peer circuit breaker tripped on consecutive failures. No series means remediation is permitted.

panels.title: Remediation skipped (rate by reason)
panels.description: Rate of automatic anti-entropy remediation passes skipped before sending any repair traffic, split by reason (opt_out, budget_exhausted, circuit_open). The drift was still detected and probed; only the repair action was suppressed. Stays at the opt_out rate until AutoRemediateOnDigestMismatch is enabled.

panels.title: Shared-dictionary compression ratio
panels.description: Achieved shared-dictionary Zstandard compression ratio on the framing encode path (FramingCompression = ZstdDictionary with a non-zero FramingCompressionDictionaryId). 'ratio' is compressed-out over uncompressed-in (lower is better; 1.0 means no saving); 'in bytes/s' and 'out bytes/s' are the before/after byte rates. Flat-zero unless shared-dictionary compression is opted into and a dictionary resolves on this silo.

panels.title: Content-hash payload elision (rate)
panels.description: Rate of Set-entry payloads and value bytes elided from outbound batches by the sender-manifest / receiver-pull-missing content-hash round trip (orleans.lattice.replication.ship.elided_payloads / ship.elided_payload_bytes). Opt-in via ContentHashDedupElisionEnabled (which also requires ContentHashDedupEnabled); flat-zero unless elision is enabled and a peer advertises the exchange capability for a duplicate-heavy workload.

panels.title: Content-hash manifest exchanges (rate)
panels.description: Rate of content-hash manifest exchanges performed with each peer on the outbound ship path (orleans.lattice.replication.ship.manifest_exchanges). One per shipped batch that advertised a manifest. Read alongside the elision panel to gauge average payloads elided per exchange and whether the pull-missing round trip is paying for itself.

panels.title: Pre-ship CRDT deltas merged (rate)
panels.description: Rate of source CRDT deltas the shipper folded into a combined delta by pre-ship coalescing (PreShipCoalescingEnabled, recognised CRDT trees). 'deltas/s' counts the same-key typed deltas merged into one combined-delta entry; pairs with the coalesce entries-elided panel which records the source entries dropped from the wire. Flat-zero unless a hot CRDT key is mutated several times within one ship window, or the tree is last-writer-wins (which elides entries without merging deltas).

panels.title: Shared-dictionary negotiation outcomes (rate)
panels.description: Rate of per-peer shared-dictionary capability negotiations by outcome (orleans.lattice.replication.ship.dictionary_negotiation). matched = the peer advertised the configured dictionary id and the sender compressed with it; fell_back = the peer advertised a capability without the configured id; unknown = the peer has not advertised a dictionary capability yet. Opt-in via DictionaryNegotiationEnabled with a ZstdDictionary tree; flat-zero unless negotiation is enabled and a shared dictionary is configured.

targets.expr: sum by (tree, peer, outcome) (rate(orleans_lattice_replication_ship_dictionary_negotiation_total{tree=~"$tree",peer=~"$peer",cluster=~"$cluster",instance=~"$silo"}[5m])) or vector(0)

panels.title: Batches shipped with vs without a shared dictionary (rate)
panels.description: Rate of batches shipped on the dictionary-eligible path split by whether a shared dictionary was used (orleans.lattice.replication.ship.dictionary_batches). with_dictionary = compressed against a negotiated shared dictionary; without_dictionary = plain dictionary-less Zstd (the fallback for a peer that has not advertised the configured id). Read alongside the negotiation-outcomes panel to confirm a mixed fleet keeps shipping during a rolling dictionary rollout.

targets.expr: sum by (tree, peer, dictionary) (rate(orleans_lattice_replication_ship_dictionary_batches_total{tree=~"$tree",peer=~"$peer",cluster=~"$cluster",instance=~"$silo"}[5m])) or vector(0)

panels.title: Receiver content-hash exchanges handled (rate)
panels.description: Rate of content-hash manifest exchanges the receiver answered for each origin peer (orleans.lattice.replication.receiver.content_manifest_exchanges). One per inbound pull-missing request handled. Pairs with the sender-side manifest-exchanges panel so an operator can confirm both ends of the round trip agree on the exchange volume. Flat-zero unless a peer ships with ContentHashDedupElisionEnabled against this receiver.

panels.title: Receiver content entries elided (rate)
panels.description: Rate of manifest entries the receiver reported it already holds byte-identical content for (orleans.lattice.replication.receiver.content_entries_elided) - the entries the receiver told the sender it does not need shipped. Pairs with the sender-side content-hash payload elision panel: the two track the same elided entries from each end of the round trip. Flat-zero unless the receiver's applied-content index is populated (ContentHashDedupEnabled) and a peer advertises the exchange.

panels.title: Receiver metadata-only HWM advances (rate)
panels.description: Rate of metadata-only per-origin high-water-mark advances the receiver performed during a content-hash exchange (orleans.lattice.replication.receiver.content_hwm_advances) - the identical-content-newer-clock idempotent re-set case where the high-water-mark advances without the payload travelling. Flat-zero unless idempotent upstream retry re-sends byte-identical content with a newer clock and the receiver already holds it.
